tasks.title: Mission leg time
tasks.solution: Accelerating to v and decelerating take v/a seconds each and together cover v²/a meters; the remaining d − v²/a is flown at v. The sum: t = d/v + v/a (if d ≥ v²/a). This is a model with no jerk limit: in SITL 4.7.2 (WP_JERK = 1 m/s³) a 100 m leg with stops at 10 m/s took 16.8–16.9 s, that is, about a/J ≈ 2.5 s more than the 14 s from the formula.

tasks.title: DO_JUMP loop
tasks.solution: param2 is the number of repeats: the first pass is flown in sequence, then r more after the jumps, r + 1 in all (in the module's run a repeat count of 1 gave two A–B passes). t = p·(r + 1) / v, divided by 60.

tasks.title: Latitude in MISSION_ITEM_INT
tasks.solution: The waypoint latitude = −35.363261 + n / 111319.5 degrees; in MISSION_ITEM_INT it is sent as an integer in degrees × 10⁷. The module's example: 100 m → −35.3623626° → −353623626. (Internally ArduPilot uses the spherical constant of 111318.845 m/°; that does not affect the answer.)
